items.claim: these tutoring blocks improve exam pass rates

cases.text: One: an algebra cohort at Brantwood College, tutored from 4 February, showed exam pass rates 7 points higher by 22 May than the previous spring term; tutor Ashworth.
Two: an algebra cohort at Brantwood College, tutored from 5 February, showed exam pass rates 5 points higher by 23 May than the previous spring term; tutor Ashworth.
Three: an algebra cohort at Brantwood College, tutored from 6 February, showed exam pass rates 8 points higher by 24 May than the previous spring term; tutor Ashworth.
Four: an algebra cohort at Brantwood College, tutored from 7 February, showed exam pass rates 4 points higher by 25 May than the previous spring term; tutor Ashworth.

items.passage:
A faculty log records four cohorts given the same tutoring blocks.
One: an algebra cohort at Brantwood College, tutored from 4 February, showed exam pass rates 7 points higher by 22 May than the previous spring term; tutor Ashworth.
Two: an algebra cohort at Brantwood College, tutored from 5 February, showed exam pass rates 5 points higher by 23 May than the previous spring term; tutor Ashworth.
The board's pass mark held exactly level with the previous term's, and every cohort sat the board's own paper under that same mark. Pass rates cover every student in each cohort, and about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block.
Three: an algebra cohort at Brantwood College, tutored from 6 February, showed exam pass rates 8 points higher by 24 May than the previous spring term; tutor Ashworth.
Four: an algebra cohort at Brantwood College, tutored from 7 February, showed exam pass rates 4 points higher by 25 May than the previous spring term; tutor Ashworth.
Results were transcribed into the faculty file and countersigned by the examinations office each week.
items.notes: All four cohorts share college, subject, term and tutor - one distinct value per dimension. Check that the closing sentence genuinely neutralises the term-over-term comparison by holding exam difficulty, grading and class size fixed, which is what makes a before/after comparison adequate here.

items.confound_note: The pass rates are tallied over "the students who attended every block", while the same line records that "about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block". The claim is about the cohorts given the tutoring blocks, so the population is every student in the cohort, not the full-attendance fraction alone. Students who attend every block are the steadiest students in a cohort and pass at higher rates whatever the tutoring did, so a 4 to 8 point rise can appear on that fraction with no change in what any student learned. All four cohorts are algebra at Brantwood College in one spring term, so the same attendance restriction applies across the four cases and none of them corrects the others.
items.notes: Cases are byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. Check that the relaxed grading works as a single confound ONLY because the four cohorts share one college and one term, and that the closer reuses the same vocabulary (grading, standards, class sizes, previous term) as the TRUE closer.
